title: Why The Sun Suddenly Explodes | Earth Science
description: Discover how invisible magnetic fields trigger massive solar flares. Learn what happens when the Sun's energy snaps and fires into deep space.
instagram_caption: Ever wonder what triggers a massive solar flare? Follow Wonders of the Nature for more.

segments.narration: Invisible magnetic ropes are pulling apart deep inside our own burning star.

segments.narration: The Sun is not just hot gas but a tangled mess of magnetism.
broll_queries: sun magnetic field animation close up

segments.narration: Imagine giant rubber bands stretching tighter until they eventually snap under the pressure.
These magnetic field lines twist into knots because the Sun rotates unevenly everywhere.
Energy builds up slowly as these field lines cross and become heavily warped.
Suddenly the tension releases and sends a massive blast of radiation toward Earth.
This flash of light travels through space reaching us in just eight minutes.
It creates a solar flare that outshines the entire Sun for brief moments.
The radiation can disrupt our satellites and blackout power grids across the planet.
Luckily our thick atmosphere protects us from feeling any of this intense heat.
These flares remain one of the most powerful explosions in our solar system.
